# Method(s) Page 2

Linear probes are linear classifiers trained on model internal representations, signalling the prescence of encoded behaviors in latent space. Specifically, linear probes use logistic regression on an LLM's activation values, with each vector labelled as behavior-present or behavior-absent. Although linear probe implementations originate in transformer-based large language models, they are not exclusive to LLMs, with certain multi-agent systems leveraging linear probes to detect encoded behaviors for white-box explainability. Behaviors such as collusion or deception have been used in multi-agent systems to reveal the behaviors presence in the latent space, even when the observable behavior does not clearly indicate so.
